caveats: Maximum likelihood by iteratively reweighted least squares, started and stopped by R glm's rules (relative change in deviance below the tolerance); standard errors from the inverse Fisher information at the estimate, and a two-sided Wald z test against the standard normal. mzLib matches R's glm(family = binomial, epsilon = 1e-14) to 1e-8 relative in coefficients and deviance, and to 1e-6 relative in standard errors and p-values, because summary.glm takes its weights from the step before the estimate. Wald tests are the least reliable of the likelihood tests near separation and in small samples; no likelihood-ratio test is offered.

separated: the design splits the feature's 0s from its 1s, so the maximum-likelihood estimate does not exist (a coefficient runs to infinity). mzLib reports the feature separated, with null statistics, when a fitted probability comes within 1E-10 of 0 or 1 (LogisticRegression.SeparationThreshold), and also when every observed outcome is the same. R's glm instead prints large, meaningless coefficients and a warning. A separated feature can be the strongest effect in the table (detected in every run of one condition and in none of another): read its events and observed counts. Firth's penalized likelihood (logistf), which gives finite estimates there, is not implemented.
p_value is not adjusted across features. Send one coefficient's p_value column to stats adjust for Benjamini-Hochberg.
Missing cells are omitted per feature, never imputed. A 0 is an outcome (for a detection table: measured as absent), not a missing value.
301 of 492 features were not fitted (301 separated); their estimate, standard_error, z, p_value and deviance are null.
